sections.heading: Core Gameplay Mechanics
sections.body:
The core gameplay mechanics of GT Ghost Racing are deceptively simple yet deeply engaging. With intuitive controls and a gradual learning curve, new players can quickly get up to speed and start competing against the ghosts. There are two main types of controls: mouse, keyboard, or touch controls. Mouse and keyboard controls are the most common, with players using the mouse to steer the vehicle and the keyboard to accelerate and brake. Touch controls are also available for players who prefer to play on mobile devices or tablets.

As you navigate the tracks, you'll need to master the art of controlling your vehicle, taking into account factors such as speed, acceleration, and braking. The game's physics engine is carefully tuned to provide a realistic and immersive experience, with particles and other visual effects adding to the overall atmosphere. With practice, you'll be able to develop a range of techniques, from smooth cornering to lightning-fast acceleration.

One of the key features of GT Ghost Racing is the rewards and penalties system. As you complete laps and collect stars, you'll earn rewards such as boosters, which give you a temporary speed boost, and shields, which protect you from obstacles and damage. However, if you crash or run out of time, you'll incur penalties, such as lost stars and reduced rewards. This system adds an extra layer of challenge and strategy to the game, as you need to carefully balance your risk and reward to achieve the best results.
